name: Jimmy Carter
description: US president associated with human-rights diplomacy, industry deregulation and energy and environmental policy.

axes.brief: Electoral accountability and post-Watergate reform supported constitutional government.
axes.counter: Judicial and executive disagreements qualified claims of absolute institutional restraint.

axes.brief: Civil liberties and legal accountability accompanied safety regulation.
axes.counter: Security powers and drug law remained despite some reform proposals.

axes.brief: Equal rights and recognition of minority communities accompanied common citizenship.
axes.counter: Inclusion did not mean every cultural practice overrode general law.

axes.brief: Refugee resettlement and humanitarian admissions expanded.
axes.counter: The Mariel crisis and numerical administration qualified unrestricted settlement.

axes.brief: Camp David, arms talks and human-rights diplomacy prioritised peaceful settlement.
axes.counter: Hostage-rescue action, defence buildup and Afghanistan-related containment qualify complete pacifism.

axes.brief: Human-rights agreements and diplomacy supported international cooperation.
axes.counter: National currency, borders and security authority remained.

axes.brief: Private enterprise and industry deregulation coexisted with public institutions.
axes.counter: Deregulation of business rules is not identical to privatising all service ownership.

axes.brief: Trade liberalisation and international economic agreements favoured openness.
Airline and other deregulation favoured market allocation.
axes.counter: Energy programmes, public health responsibilities and legal wage floors remained.

axes.brief: Welfare reform and employment support aimed at poverty while fiscal restraint limited expansion.
axes.counter: Reform proposals did not all pass; opportunity and benefits were not unrestricted equalisation.

axes.brief: Church–state separation and religious freedom coexisted with personal Baptist conviction.
axes.counter: Public religious tradition is distinct from clergy reviewing civil law.

axes.brief: Women’s equality and the ERA were supported while abortion views were personally restrictive.
axes.counter: His later public positions are excluded; social reform was not uniform across sexuality and reproduction.

axes.brief: Energy conservation and protected Alaskan lands constrained resource development.
axes.counter: Energy technology and beneficial infrastructure were also supported.

axes.brief: National energy and education initiatives coexisted with state constitutions and local police.
axes.counter: Federal standards did not eliminate ordinary state government.

axes.brief: Education, discrimination and social opportunity supplied behavioural context.
axes.counter: No complete genetics doctrine was identified; exact comparisons remain provisional.
